scenes.title: The plan
scenes.vo: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Narrower ranges earn more fees per dollar while in range and go out of range sooner. the calculator Every rebalance costs gas and swap fees and locks in the impermanent loss so far. Professionals set a rule before entering: $2,400 to $3,600 (±20%): about 10.4 times. $2,700 to $3,300 (±10%): about 20.4 times. $2,850 to $3,150 (±5%): about 40.5 times.
scenes.cap: Narrower ranges earn more fees per dollar while in range and go out of range sooner. the calculator Every rebalance costs gas and swap fees and locks in the impermanent loss so far. scenes.title: Worked example
steps: A ±5% range would be out of range most weeks.
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. ETH typically moves ±7% a week. A ±5% range would be out of range most weeks. The rule points to ±10 to 12%: about 20 times efficiency, and time in range to earn.
scenes.cap: Let's work an example, step by step. ETH typically moves ±7% a week. A ±5% range would be out of range most weeks. The rule points to ±10–12%: ~20× efficiency, and time in range to earn.

scenes.title: Checklist
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, Width at least 1.5 times typical weekly move. Next, Rebalance trigger and invalidation written. Then, Rebalance cost budget set. And finally, P and L tracked against holding (Lesson 2.4).
scenes.cap: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, Width ≥ 1.5× typical weekly move. Next, Rebalance trigger and invalidation written. Then, Rebalance cost budget set. And finally, P&L tracked against holding (Lesson 2.4).

scenes.q: Why does a ±5% range earn ~2× the fees of ±10% while in range?
scenes.a: The same capital is concentrated in half the price range, so it provides about twice the liquidity there.
scenes.vo: Question one. Why does a ±5% range earn about 2 times the fees of ±10% while in range? [[pause 4]] The answer: The same capital is concentrated in half the price range, so it provides about twice the liquidity there.
scenes.cap: Question 1. Why does a ±5% range earn ~2× the fees of ±10% while in range? The answer: The same capital is concentrated in half the price range, so it provides about twice the liquidity there.

scenes.q: What does a rebalance lock in?
scenes.a: The impermanent loss accrued so far, plus gas and swap costs.
scenes.vo: Question two. What does a rebalance lock in? [[pause 4]] The answer: The impermanent loss accrued so far, plus gas and swap costs.
scenes.cap: Question 2. What does a rebalance lock in? The answer: The impermanent loss accrued so far, plus gas and swap costs.

scenes.q: Price breaks structure and exits the range. Re-centre?
scenes.a: No. That's an invalidation. Exit per plan.
